description:
Toast of Broadway Toastmasters welcomes anyone who would like to improve their speaking skills to join our meetings. No previous experience is necessary - come and share your experiences with us!

At Toast of Broadway we like to balance having fun, learning and building a community. Every meeting you will have the chance to speak on the stage and try out a variety of speaking roles. Come along to see what we're all about!

For more than 25 years we have offered our members a proven and enjoyable way to practice their communication skills.

"Join Toastmasters. Oral communication skills count! " - Tom Peters, Author

Our Club is part of Toastmasters International's network of over 13,000 clubs that meet in 113 countries around the world.

Toastmasters is a non-profit organisation which provides a forum for people to improve their speaking and leadership skills. Our members come from all walks of life which offers participants a great opportunity for networking.

Meetings are non-political, non-religious, and open to anyone 18 years or older. We have heaps of free car parking at the spaces around the building marked as 'Jubilee".

Many professional bodies recognize the time spent In Toastmasters towards their membership Continuing Professional Development (CPD) Hours requirement E.g. Lawyers, Chartered Accountants. Please check with your relevant bodies for further details.

Follow us on Facebook at https://www.facebook.com/toastbroadway

For more information visit out website https://toastofbroadway.org.nz

title: Green Prescription Trail
location: Auckland Botanic Gardens, 102 Hill Road, Manurewa, Auckland, Auckland
description:
Botanic Gardens Week 2026 celebrates the health and wellbeing benefits of botanic gardens and arboreta, recognising the now undeniable truth that nature is medicine.
This May, visit Auckland Botanic Gardens and experience the proven benefits first-hand with our Green Prescription Trail.
Botanic gardens are uniquely placed to support health and wellbeing because they:

provide accessible spaces
promote physical activity
restore mental health
foster social connection
strengthen our bond with nature.

All of which are proven to increase overall wellbeing.​
A growing body of research shows that spending time in nature measurably improves human health. ​​Studies demonstrate that even a 20-30 minute walk in a green space can:

lower cortisol levels
reduce blood pressure
improve mood
boost cognitive performance.

From Japan’s 'shinrin-yoku' (forest bathing) research to UK public health trials, it’s shown that immersive plant-rich environments help:

decrease anxiety
restore attention
enhance creativity
improve recovery outcomes for people living with chronic illness.

Australian research echoes this, confirming that access to green spaces is associated with reduced psychological distress and improved mental wellbeing.

description:
Hi Architects,

Welcome to the next [AWS Auckland Well Architected User Group](https://www.meetup.com/aws-canberra-well-architected-user-group/) Meetup of 2026!

At each meetup, we focus on learning and networking in a friendly and inclusive atmosphere and explore best-practices in AWS. This has resulted in the AWS Well-Architected Meetups becoming the most popular AWS Meetups in ANZ 🥳

**Please also note that AWS Security now requests a company name and company email where it is available. If you are a student, please list your institution and your student email address at that institution 👍**

* **Yadwinder Sharma, Founder, https://www.nimbal.ai**

**From 5 Days to 5 Minutes: Reimagining Well-Architected QA with Autonomous AI**

Modern software delivery is accelerating faster than traditional QA can keep up. Teams are facing rising costs, delayed releases and significant reputational risks when quality is compromised. At the same time, AI-generated code and rapid release cycles are outpacing manual testing capabilities.

This session explores how autonomous, cloud-native QA powered by AI agents is transforming software verification—reducing testing time from days to minutes and costs from thousands to tens of dollars, supported by AWS Well-Architected principles of:

Operational Excellence: Automating QA workflows with self-service, zero-setup AI agents
Reliability: Detecting broken links, errors and performance issues before production
Cost Optimization: Moving from high fixed QA costs to on-demand, per-run pricing models and more

title: I Was There!
location: Central City Library, 44-46 Lorne Street, Auckland City Centre, Auckland, Auckland
description:
I Was There! celebrates one man’s deep love of live music in Tāmaki Makaurau. This exhibition brings together original gig posters and handwritten set lists from shows attended between 1990 and 1995 - a golden era for New Zealand music fans.
Featuring legendary acts such as The 3Ds, Straitjacket Fits, Able Tasmans, Tall Dwarfs and many more. Each piece is paired with a short personal reflection that captures what it felt like to be in the room on the night.
Curated by longtime gig‑goer Paul Rowe, who has attended hundreds of shows over his lifetime, the exhibition reflects a time when NZ live music was thriving - played loud and late in iconic venues, some of which have since disappeared.
Step back into the 1990s, relive the sweat, noise and moments that mattered. Bring your own musical memories along and reconnect with the gigs this May.
